name: Acute Interstitial Pneumonia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Acute Interstitial Pneumonia

criteria.description: Acute onset of respiratory failure with rapid progression
Diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities and consolidation on chest imaging
Diffuse alveolar damage on lung biopsy
Exclusion of known causes of acute lung injury including infection, drug toxicity, and connective tissue disease
No prior history or evidence of chronic interstitial lung disease

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All major criteria including acute respiratory failure, characteristic imaging, diffuse alveolar damage on biopsy, and exclusion of other causes must be met
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Lung biopsy is often required to confirm diagnosis; rapid clinical deterioration is typical

pathognomonic.symptomName: Diffuse bilateral crackles on lung auscultation

laboratory: Hypoxemia on arterial blood gas analysis
Normal or mildly elevated white blood cell count
imaging: Diffuse bilateral ground-glass opacities on chest CT
other: Diffuse alveolar damage pattern on lung biopsy
Exclusion of infectious etiologies by microbiological studies

distinguishingFeatures: Known precipitating cause such as sepsis or trauma
More common in critically ill patients
Histopathology overlaps but clinical context differs
Presence of organizing pneumonia pattern on biopsy
Usual interstitial pneumonia pattern on imaging and biopsy

redFlags: Rapid progression to respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation
Severe hypoxemia refractory to oxygen therapy
Diffuse alveolar damage on lung biopsy
references: American Thoracic Society/European Respiratory Society International Multidisciplinary Consensus Classification of the Idiopathic Interstitial Pneumonias, Am J Respir Crit Care Med. 2002
Acute Interstitial Pneumonia: Clinical Features and Outcomes, Chest. 2010
Diffuse Alveolar Damage and Acute Interstitial Pneumonia, Respir Med. 2015
